Playbook.name: Change Audit — Windows System Time Changed by an Interactive Account - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: System time was changed (4616) by an interactive account (machine/SYSTEM/service excluded). Triage question: benign time-sync/admin action, or an attacker skewing time to disrupt logs/Kerberos/forensics?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Time manipulation can break Kerberos, misalign logs to frustrate forensics, and trigger security-control failures.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the time change is a benign admin/sync action or deliberate time skew.

Step.name: Time-change detail and magnitude
Step.Purpose: A small adjustment is benign sync; a large jump (hours/days) is suspicious.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4616" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.PreviousTime, winlog.event_data.NewTime, winlog.event_data.ProcessName | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: Compare PreviousTime vs NewTime: seconds = benign sync; a large jump is suspicious. ProcessName tells you the tool (w32tm/svchost = sync; cmd/powershell = manual).

Step.name: Did suspicious activity surround the time change on this host
Step.Purpose: Time skew paired with security-relevant activity (log clear, privilege use) indicates anti-forensics.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("1102","4672","4688","7045") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code) | LIMIT 5
Step.AnalystNotes: A log clear (1102) or service install near the time change supports anti-forensics; a quiet host supports benign sync.

Node.Condition: Large time jump by an interactive account via a manual tool, especially near a log-clear/privilege event.
Small adjustment by w32tm/sync process, or an admin correcting drift under a ticket.
Time changed by an admin with no ticket and unclear magnitude.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-TIME-CHANGE, INV-02-TIME-CONTEXT to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Benign time synchronisation or an authorised correction.

TruePositive.Definition: Deliberate time skew to disrupt logs/Kerberos/forensics.

SOCAction.Item: Restore correct time; isolate if anti-forensics; open IR.
Reconstruct the affected window from SIEM.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A misconfigured NTP client causing repeated corrections.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
